concerns.text: T010 ('Execute the complete pipeline end-to-end on the full 500-task set and all configurations') is ordered AFTER T008/T009, which already analyze the sweep logs. If T010 re-executes the pipeline, the analysis_report.json / sensitivity_report.json produced in T008/T009 become stale relative to T010's run, violating the producer-before-consumer flow. The authoritative full execution must precede the analysis tasks (or T010 must be re-scoped to verification-only with no re-execution).

T008's granularity-validation sweep requires agent executions on a 'denser 10-unit library-size grid on a task subset', but no task before T008 produces those runs — T007's sweep only covers sizes {10,30,50,100}. T008 is an analysis-only task with no producer for this input; either a producer task (agent runs at 10-unit increments) must precede T008, or T008 must explicitly include invoking the agent for the dense grid.

Execution order states 'T011–T013 partially parallel', but T012 must reference 'figure files' that only T011 generates. T012 should be explicitly sequenced after T011 (or the parallelism note scoped to T013 only) to avoid a consumer-before-producer within Phase 3.

T004's verification validates against contracts/experiment_log.schema.yaml, which is created in T001; T004 is listed as parallel with T003 but its dependency on T001 is implicit. Harmless given T001 is first, but the stated order 'T003/T004 (parallel)' should note both depend on T001/T002 outputs where applicable (T003 on T002's data files is stated; T004 on T001's schema is not).
